feature: Ask draws a thing you can tell at a glance
summary: Ask a blank picture for a dog, a cat, a coffee cup or a smiley face icon and you get a clean, recognizable drawing made of editable layers, one group named for the thing. Ask looks at the drawing with a model that can see before it hands back, and draws it again (twice at most) or says it could not.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no switch changed from its default. Needs Ollama with qwen3:30b (Ask's planner) and llama3.2-vision (the look); both are on this Mac. Walk: Scripts/playtest/ask-draws-a-dog-walk.json.

try.do: File > New Blank Canvas, Desktop size, then press Ask.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Type: draw a picture of a dog. Press Return and wait about 20 seconds.
Open the Dog group in Layers and pick an ear or a leg: each part is its own shape.
Press Command Z once: the whole dog goes.
Press Ask again and type: create a smiley face icon.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Export the icon as SVG and open it: ellipses for the face and eyes, one path for the smile.
Ask for something less everyday, a lighthouse, and see what it says.
Look at the before and after sheet of all thirteen requests.

evaluate: Would you show the dog, the cat and the smiley to someone without apologising?
Is borrowing a clean built-in drawing for an everyday thing what you want, or do you expect Ask to draw it from scratch every time?
On a blank picture, is turning the whole picture into the 512 point icon frame the right answer to 'make an icon'?
For a thing it cannot draw well (the lighthouse), is 'I couldn't make a clear drawing of that. Nothing was changed.' better than leaving its best try?
Is about 18 seconds from Ask to the drawing fast enough?

measured.eval: Scripts/ask-eval.sh, the 13 drawing cases, each on a blank 1440 x 1024 picture at Next defaults, judged blind by a model that did not draw it (3 looks each)

before.namedBlind: 1 of 13 (2 by a majority of the three looks)

after.namedBlind: 13 of 13 (coffee cup 2 of 3: the third look said hot coffee)

measured.rules: Every after case scored 10 of 10 on the read document: on the canvas, centred, no stray words; the smiley icon has 2 eyes and a mouth, each inside the face, on a square canvas.
measured.offTheSet: Things the built-in set lacks (run 20261020-185749-ask, not kept in the history): a giraffe wearing a scarf read right first time; a lighthouse and a windmill were drawn three times by the model and refused by the look each time, so Ask said it could not and changed nothing (179 s and 107 s).

rough: No mock covers what a drawing looks like; the Ask panel and composer are unchanged apart from the closing sentence when a drawing does not read.

Things outside the built-in set are still weak: the local model's own SVG of a lighthouse or a windmill never read as one, and three tries take up to three minutes before Ask gives up. Folded into an-illustration-ask-draws-looks-illustrated-natu, which already asks for a lighthouse and a fox drawn with craft.

Everyday things come from Twemoji's drawings (CC-BY 4.0, credited in Open Source Notices), so a dog looks like the emoji dog. They are full drawings made of shapes, recolourable part by part, not pictures.
The Agent row reads 'Drew a drawing' rather than naming the thing.
Parts of a built-in drawing are named only for faces (Face, Left eye, Right eye, Mouth); a dog's parts are Dog 1 to Dog 12.
The first look after the Mac has been idle takes about 12 seconds while the seeing model loads; after that a look is a few seconds.
Networking off was checked by construction, not by pulling the cable: Ask calls only 127.0.0.1 (Ollama), and the drawings ship inside the app. The eval's judge needs the network, Ask does not.
